title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Meridian Logistics
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in. Customer interested in upgrading reserved capacity to support peak holiday throughput, adding EU and APAC regions for lower latency, and discussing a 12-month extension with committed spend. Security/compliance questions about SOC 2, KMS and audit logs. Redwood to send updated quote and SOC2/arch docs; schedule a short benchmark next week on dedicated pool.
next_steps: Jordan to send updated pricing and committed-capacity quote by 2027-01-03
Samira to share runbook and SOC2 + KMS architecture docs by 2026-12-30
Customer to approve pilot nodes and schedule benchmark (target week of 2027-01-04)
action_items: Jordan Blake: prepare expanded dedicated quote + region add-on, due 2027-01-03
Samira Khan: export SOC2 report excerpt & KMS integration diagram, due 2026-12-30
Priya Patel: provide expected Q1 traffic spike numbers and PKI team contact, due 2027-01-02
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Evan Li (Redwood CSM), Carlos Ruiz (Meridian Head of ML), Priya Patel (Meridian Infrastructure Lead), Leo Martins (Meridian CTO)

Auto-summary (may be rough): quick renewal check, expansion ask for EU + APAC regions, asking about dedicated capacity bump for holiday peaks and potential 12-month contract extension. Security questions around SOC 2 and KMS.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody, thanks for jumping on, um, happy holidays, we'll keep this tight - agenda is renewal and expansion, quick perf check, and next steps. Carlos you on mute?
[00:12] Carlos: yeah sorry, I'm on - thanks Jordan. we've been happy overall, but holiday season bumped us higher than expected, and we wanna talk about capacity and adding regions.
[00:24] Samira: quick clarifying q, are you expecting sustained Q1 increase or mostly spikes around shipments window?
[00:32] Carlos: mostly spikes, we've got peak routing ops and customer chatbots, so bursts where latency really matters. we saw some tails on request latency in APAC because your hosted region's farther.
[00:44] Priya: and also want to align on data residency for EU customers - legal asked for logs retention and KMS key control.
[00:55] Jordan: got it. high level from redwood's side: we can propose a reserved/dedicated bump - add two extra dedicated pods in our dedicated offering, and we can spin up region replicas in eu-west and ap-sg. depends on commit level.
[01:08] Leo: what's the lead time for region bring-up? we need this before next peak in mid-Jan.
[01:15] Samira: lead time typically 5-7 business days for dedicated pools in a new region if capacity's available; if not, we can do burst routing to a compatible lower-cap model while we provision.
[01:28] Carlos: and cost delta? like, per-token and reserved monthly?
[01:33] Jordan: for committed capacity we'll do monthly reserved pricing; rough ballpark - adding two extra xlarge pods is ~1.8x current committed spend, but unit token cost drops because of batching and prefix caching. I'll put exact numbers in the quote.
[01:46] Priya: we need that quote to present to procurement - also want the SLA updates if we're adding regions and cross-region failover.
[01:55] Evan: on SLAs we can extend the uptime SLO to include regional availability, and outline failover behaviour - can be part of the SOW extension.
[02:06] Carlos: ok, also concerns around private deployment - we discussed private (VPC/on-prem) earlier, is that still on the table?
[02:14] Samira: yes, private is an option; for your use case we recommended dedicated first as it's faster to deploy; private deployments require change window and infra prep.
[02:25] Priya: security heavy lifting - do you support customer-managed KMS / HSM?
[02:30] Samira: yes, we integrate with customer KMS; HSM via partner integrations for the highest level. we'll share the integration diagram.
[02:38] Carlos: sweet. what about audit logs and retention? procurement wants 12 months of logs, but also ability to pull them on-demand.
[02:46] Evan: we can export audit logs to a customer-owned storage endpoint, or provide extended retention as an add-on. will include options.
[02:55] Leo: performance question - can you commit to P99 latency targets with increased token rates? we saw P99 at ~820ms last month for some routes.
[03:07] Samira: with dedicated and regional placement we expect P99 to drop below 400-500ms for typical chat seq len 256; for heavy long-form generation we can tweak kernel selection, quantization and batching. but we should run a benchmark with your representative workload.
[03:24] Carlos: yes please, we'll provide workloads. when can we run it?
[03:28] Jordan: target next week - Samira can provision a small dedicated pool and we run the benchmark with your dataset.
[03:34] Priya: timeline wise we need an updated contract in hand by the first week of Jan to get procurement sign-off.
[03:41] Jordan: understood. high priority is quote + SOC2 + KMS docs. Samira?
[03:45] Samira: I'll export the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration diagram tonight and send by tomorrow EOD, worst case Monday.
[03:53] Carlos: small note, some names in the doc sometimes spell Redwood's product names wrong - engineering wants exact model names for the benchmark, like which quantized variant you'll route to.
[04:03] Samira: noted - we'll include model catalog names and the exact runtime flags used.
[04:10] Evan: also adding a paragraph about observability - token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing - procurement likes that.
[04:17] Leo: any blocker on contract term? we're thinking 12-month extension with a modest uplift for committed capacity, maybe a year start on Feb 1.
[04:26] Jordan: that aligns. we can do a 12-month renewal with a committed capacity addendum; we'll propose tiered commit levels so you can pick between small/medium/large bumps.
[04:38] Carlos: will you include add-on pricing for EU and APAC regions? we need region-by-region pricing to show ops team.
[04:45] Jordan: yes, region add-ons will be line items. also include estimated provisioning lead times per region.
[04:52] Priya: quick syscall about backups - if we bring in private or VPC option, what about VPC peering and egress costs?
[04:59] Samira: VPC peering is supported; egress costs are typically pass-through and we'll estimate in the quote.
[05:06] Carlos: who will own the KPI during the pilot? we want a joint success plan.
[05:11] Evan: Redwood CSM will own tracking and we'll define success criteria - target latency, availability during spikes, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:19] Jordan: to recap next steps: I'll send pricing/commit options by Jan 3; Samira will send SOC2/KMS/arch docs by Dec 30; we schedule a benchmark/pilot next week - customer to share workload samples and target windows. any other blockers?
[05:33] Priya: procurement asked for references from another logistics customer if possible.
[05:37] Jordan: we can provide a redacted reference, I'll follow up.
[05:41] Carlos: that's all for us, thanks folks.
[05:44] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and set the benchmark slot. end.
